text:
Buffalo visits Toronto tonight with the better underlying numbers and the worse results. The Sabres create 3.03 expected goals per 60 and allow 2.84, while the Maple Leafs sit at 3.00 and 3.77. Yet Buffalo is giving up 3.57 goals a game against Toronto's 3.14. Toronto has controlled just 43 percent of the quality chances at five-on-five to Buffalo's 55, and the Leafs have been outchanced in each of their last five games despite going 2-3 with two of those losses coming past regulation. The model sees an even game, 3.13 expected goals for Buffalo and 3.08 for Toronto. Both teams played Tuesday, so rest is level.

Special teams lean Toronto's way on the power play (0.77 expected goals per game against 0.55), but the Leafs' penalty kill is shakier, allowing 0.95 per game to Buffalo's 0.77. Toronto also takes more penalties (4.14 a game) than it draws (3.86), while Buffalo draws 4.43 and takes 3.71, so the Sabres should get their share of chances with the man advantage.

The goalie matchup is a study in contrasts. Sergei Bobrovsky is projected for Toronto, and he has saved 4.65 goals above expected in four games after a rough last season (minus 13.5 over 52 games). Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is projected for Buffalo and has struggled so far, with a .850 save percentage and minus 3.84 goals saved above expected, though he was a strong 9.12 over 35 games last year. Among skaters, the model likes Tage Thompson most for Buffalo, at 39 percent to score, with Jack Quinn at 27. For Toronto, William Nylander and Auston Matthews are both at 38 percent to score and 30 percent to record two or more points.
